label: Looks and voice
rationale: Describing what someone looks and sounds like: tall, short, loud, long hair, a good figure.
mixUps: Each noun picks its own size word: height is takai/hikui (never ookii or mijikai), hair is nagai, and a loud voice is ookii, since koe ga takai means high-pitched. sutairu ga ii is a good figure, not fashion (that's oshare).

targets.trap: Not kare wa takai: takai on its own is for things (high, expensive), so a person's height needs se ga takai.
targets.use: The plain way to call someone tall: ano hito, se takai ne, with ga dropped in casual speech. Before a noun, ga often becomes no: se no takai hito (a tall person).
targets.notes: Sei ga takai is a common spoken variant. The 'tall' sense of takai applies to a person only inside this phrase. For an exact height, use shinchou: shinchou nan senchi? (how tall are you?).

example.romaji: uchi no ani, se takai n da.

examplePolite.romaji: uchi no ani wa se ga takai n desu.
examplePolite.ja: うちの兄は背が高いんです。

targets.trap: Not se ga mijikai: in Japanese height is high or low, so short is hikui. Mijikai is for length and duration, never height.
targets.use: The opposite of se ga takai, often said about yourself: watashi, se hikui kara... Casual speech drops ga.
targets.notes: Casual speech also says chiisai (chiisai hito); chibi is teasing slang.

example.romaji: watashi, se hikui kara, ue no tana todokanai n da.
example.ja: 私、背低いから、上の棚届かないんだ。
example.english: I'm short, so I can't reach the top shelf.

examplePolite.romaji: watashi wa se ga hikui node, ue no tana ni todokanai n desu.
examplePolite.ja: 私は背が低いので、上の棚に届かないんです。
examplePolite.english: I'm short, so I can't reach the top shelf.

targets.english: have a loud voice, be loud
targets.verbSense: ookii: big; for sounds and voices, loud
targets.trap: Not koe ga takai, which in everyday speech means high-pitched. urusai also works for 'you're being noisy', but it sounds annoyed (urusai! = shut up) and calls the person noisy or nagging, not their voice loud. To describe a loud voice, say koe ga ookii (casually koe dekai).
targets.use: Said about someone who talks loudly (ano hito, koe ookii yo ne) or to quieten someone: chotto, koe ookii! Casual speech drops ga, and friends often say koe dekai (dekai is blunter and more slangy than ookii). The opposite, koe ga chiisai, means quiet or soft-spoken (koe chiisai yo = speak up, I can't hear you).
targets.notes: 'Speak up' is motto ookii koe de, and 'in a loud voice' is ookina koe de. In older speech and period dramas, shh, koe ga takai! means 'keep your voice down'.

examplePolite.romaji: sumimasen, chotto koe ga ookii desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: すみません、ちょっと声が大きいですよ。
examplePolite.english: Excuse me, you're being a bit loud.

targets.trap: Not nagai kami o motte iru ('has long hair'): Japanese doesn't 'have' hair. Say kami ga nagai, the same frame as se ga takai, or nagai kami o shite iru, nagai kami no hito.
targets.use: Describes someone's hair in the person wa kami ga nagai frame: imouto, kami nagai yo, with ga dropped. Before a noun ga becomes no (kami no nagai hito), and 'your hair's got long' is kami nobita ne.
targets.notes: Short hair is kami ga mijikai, but people often just say shooto (shooto ni shita = I went short).

example.romaji: imouto, kami nagai n da yo.
example.english: My little sister's got long hair.

examplePolite.romaji: imouto wa kami ga nagai n desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 妹は髪が長いんですよ。
examplePolite.english: My younger sister has long hair.

targets.trap: False friend: sutairu ga ii is about the body, not fashion. To praise how someone dresses, say oshare or fuku no sensu ga ii.
targets.use: A common compliment on someone's figure, usually meaning slim and well-proportioned: sutairu ii ne, with ga dropped. It's said of men and women alike, and an amazing figure is sutairu batsugun.
targets.notes: For a toned build, kitaeteru ne (you work out, don't you) is the usual compliment.

example.ja: スタイルいいね！モデルみたい。
example.english: You've got a great figure! Like a model.

examplePolite.romaji: sutairu ga ii desu ne! moderu mitai desu.
examplePolite.ja: スタイルがいいですね！モデルみたいです。
examplePolite.english: You have a great figure! You look like a model.

reviewPool.english: put up (open) an umbrella; have an umbrella up
